item.title: Max Clark Explains Why Detroit Fits His Game
item.description: Detroit Tigers outfielder Max Clark described the kind of player he is in a clip MLB Network posted, and he put the grit first. “I feel like I have that gritty – there’s some flash in there, but I play hard and I’ll run in your face, I’ll throw you out, I’ll hit a homer and play defense,” Clark said in the clip, which Tigers On SI transcribed . Clark was describing Detroit when he got to that line. “It’s a city where everyone works hard, grinds and wants to come together as one big city. I feel like I have that in my game,” he said. “It’s a little bit of everything, but it’s all based on hard work and determination to be better than you and I think that’s what the backbone of that city is built off of.” "It's a city where everyone works hard, grinds and wants to come together as one big city. I feel like I have that in my game…" @maxxclarkk13 shares why his play style is a fit in Detroit 🐯 pic.twitter.com/bfWVaZuTnC — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 3, 2026 Detroit Tigers center fielder Max Clark (15) bats against Pittsburgh Pirates during the fifth inning at Comerica Park in Detroit on Friday, Sept. 25, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Max Clark Had a Solid 2026 Season for the Detroit Tigers Clark played 51 games for Detroit in 2026 after making his debut on July 31 against the Athletics , a 13-1 win in which he went 3-for-4 with two doubles. He hit .272 with three home runs and 23 RBIs, and he stole five bases on six attempts. Clark finished with a .350 on-base percentage, a .417 slugging percentage and a .766 OPS. He is 21 years old. Clark Needs to Be an Everyday Outfielder in 2027 When opening day 2027 arrives for Detroit, Clark has to be one of the three starting outfielders. Riley Greene will be another starter in the outfield. With questions about Kerry Carpenter and Parker Meadows, Clark is clearly better than those two players. The Tigers want their young players to contribute. Center field is the opening. Meadows started 11 of the Tigers’ first 13 games there in 2026 before an April 9 collision with Greene sent him to the hospital, and Clark is the center fielder on Detroit’s depth chart now. Prospect Zyhir Hope , who came to Detroit from the Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, is another player who could crack the Tigers outfield at some point in 2027. However, Clark and Kevin McGonigle are two young players in Detroit who play with swagger, and both are cornerstone pieces for the long haul.

item.description: Feb 19, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņġis (7) comes in as a substitute against the Boston Celtics during the second quarter at Chase Center. The latest win was a 120-100 victory over the Miami Heat , which was the team’s sixth straight on the road, and that turnaround gives the Warriors a little bit more breathing room. But the front office is still facing a lot of huge calls in any deal involving Porzingis. And according to Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints , the Warriors have contacted the Milwaukee Bucks , Chicago Bulls , and New Orleans Pelicans about a deal involving Porzingis. He has been away from the Warriors since training camp and hasn’t played or practiced this season at all. The 31-year-old has a disclosed diagnosis of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, also known as POTS. And ESPN’s Shams Charania and Anthony Slater reported that he might be leaning toward retirement as well, but there still hasn’t been a decision, and there is no timetable for his return. And that is why these talks are primarily about his contract. The Warriors are looking for someone to help carry them this season, while an acquiring team would have to be comfortable with the possibility that Porzingis never plays a game for them. Milwaukee might be the most interesting call . Siegel reported that the Bucks are willing to move Myles Turner in a Porzingis deal, but they would want draft capital back in return. The Warriors apparently see it the other way around. If taking on Turner’s contract means sending Porzingis and another player to make this move, they would want Milwaukee to offer something extra to make the deal work. Myles Turner would definitely give Stephen Curry a center who can protect the rim and stretch the floor, but he’s owed $28 million next season and also has a $29.1 million player option for 2028-29. That is a very different proposition if the Warriors also have to give up a rotation player or picks. The Warriors have also contacted Chicago about Jalen Smith . The Pelicans have been identified as the least concrete of the three possibilities. The Warriors have reportedly contacted the Pelicans, but there hasn’t been a player discussed in those talks. So for now, Chicago offers a specific target, while the New Orleans call might be worth revisiting near the trade deadline. The interest makes a lot of sense when you look at Porzingis’ contract. item.title: ‘Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years,’: Knicks set the record straight after players named her ‘fakest celebrity fan’
item.description: Jun 10, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Taylor Swift reacts after the New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in game four of the 2026 NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Taylor Swift caught some unexpected shade from a pair of New York Knicks players this week, who named her the team’s fakest celebrity fan. But it turns out that the Knicks organization doesn’t see it that way. On Friday, the Knicks released a statement backing Swift, making it clear that they appreciate her support. The statement came less than a day after Tyler Kolek and Miles “Deuce” McBride questioned her fandom during a livestream. ‘Fakest celebrity fan’ Kolek and McBride were playing NBA 2K during a TikTok livestream on Thursday when they were asked to name the fakest celebrity Knicks fan. Kolek floated Swift’s name , though he acknowledged that her busy schedule might keep her from attending more games. “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Kolek said. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” McBride agreed with his teammate’s pick. “I would agree,” McBride said. “Swifties not gonna like that answer.” The pair also suggested that Swift’s appearances at Madison Square Garden were “a little performative.” Instead, they gave their seal of approval to regulars like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan, who they approved of as real fans of the team. It wasn’t the first time that Swift’s Knicks fandom has been questioned. During the NBA Finals, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy said he was “sick of her” after she attended games. Knicks Respond The Knicks didn’t waste much time responding. Hours after the livestream, the team reached out to TMZ Sports with a statement. “Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” the Knicks said, via TMZ . Swift’s history with the Knicks goes back more than two decades. According to TMZ, she sang at the Garden as part of a Knicks halftime kids’ talent contest in 2003, when she was 13, and she has said that’s when she became a fan. She was also courtside for the Knicks’ historic Game 4 comeback in the NBA Finals in June, on the way to the franchise’s first championship in 53 years. And of course, she and Travis Kelce got married at Madison Square Garden in July. Needless to say, it’s going to be hard to convince the Knicks that Swift isn’t a real fan. Arizona shouldn’t stop there. Josh Sweat is one of the hottest names on the trade market, with the Dallas Cowboys (who would be on this list if they didn’t play in the NFC East) rumored to be one of his suitors. The Cardinals should be able to get back strong draft capital, led by as high as a second-round pick (at least third-round value), in a trade for the edge rusher who had 12 sacks and four forced fumbles last season. Eight-time Pro Bowl safety Budda Baker and two-time Pro Bowl running back James Conner are other names that should draw trade interest. The Cardinals, 3-5, are coming off a stunning comeback road win at Dallas and have looked better than expected in Mike LaFleur’s first year as head coach. item.title: Preseason Thunder will not return to Daytona in 2027
item.description: Motorsport photo Fans have been calling for the return of Preseason Thunder at Daytona International Speedway, which served as a pre-season test and the first glimpse of new driver/team combinations. In April, NASCAR's John Probst indicated that a January test at Daytona was likely to return, but plans have since changed. The original plan was to use the test to improve the superspeedway package, but NASCAR now appears more satisfied with the current package after recent changes to the spoiler and horsepower over the summer. NASCAR still sees areas to address, especially in regards to extreme fuel-saving, which has become a major feature of the opening stages at superspeedway races. However, NASCAR CEO Steve O'Donnell said NASCAR currently has no plans to hold the test . General view General view “On our end, you look at the changes we’ve made, and this goes back to our competition group, we’ve said we’re going to move fast," said O'Donnell. "I think historically at NASCAR we would have said, we’ll see in 2027 and we’ll talk about the short track package in 2028. That’s not the case. We moved quickly. From an on-track competition car, are you able to move and do some different things directionally? I think we’re comfortable with heading to Daytona with what we saw. "Now, kind of the officiating or sporting regulations, I think we are taking a look at. With technology, with AI, it's become such a focus on fuel-saving. If you ask the drivers if they ever fuel saved at Talladega ten years ago, the answer is yes. That's always happened. But it's become such a focus now on what you can do and the strategy in the race. "That is the focus in terms of how does the actual race play out, not necessarily the car, but what does the race look like in terms of is it stages or whatever we may do during the race. "But we don't have plans right now to go test at Daytona." item.title: Vasseur’s Message to Hamilton and Leclerc After Mexico: ‘Ferrari Is Coming First’
item.description: Frederic Vasseur says he met Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Brazil after their Mexico clash with one message: Ferrari comes first. Ferrari team boss Vasseur confirmed the meeting with Hamilton and Leclerc in Brazil ahead of F1 weekend, following their moment in Mexico and the Brit’s verbal outburst . The Frenchman didn’t wish to expand on what was discussed, but he said it was a positive talk. Vasseur reminded the two who they raced for and how they should behave. He didn’t dwell as much on what Mercedes boss Toto Wolff used to do when handling Hamilton and Nico Rosberg back in the day when they collided often. Vasseur Met Them on Thursday Evening “We did it yesterday evening because I had to fly back to Europe between the two races, but it went well,” said Vasseur in Friday’s press conference. “It was good to discuss, good to clarify my position and their position. It was good to do, and now we turn the page, and we are focused on the next one.” Asked by Sky’s Ted Kravitz whether the drivers had agreed to work together for a Ferrari win, Vasseur said the conclusion of the meeting was “a clear reminder that the Ferrari is coming first. It’s coming first for the brand, for the employees, for the tifosi, and this we have to keep in mind.” “First, I’m not sure that Toto 10 years ago told you exactly the content of the discussion with Nico and Lewis, and I will do exactly the same: we had a discussion. It has to stay private. It’s a matter of respect also for them and for the team, and, once again, the most important thing is the message. The message is that we are working for a brand. “We are working for sponsors, we are working for, but I would say probably mainly also the employees of the team, and we had a good recovery in terms of performance. We came back after Madrid in much better shape, and this is due to the work of the people at home. “And we are all, as a team, we all have to keep this in mind that it’s not due to the wind or whatever. It’s due to the work of the people and the employees of the company, and it was the tone of the message,” summed up Vasseur. He also questioned whether Hamilton had really said Leclerc races him harder than his previous teammates. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton. item.title: Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy: Abhimanyu Easwaran to captain as Bengal name 19-member squad
item.description: KOLKATA: Bengal decided to bank on youngsters as they picked Under-23 skipper Shashank Singh for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali (T20) tournament. Another youngster, former Royal Challengers Bengaluru bowler Prayas Ray Barman also made a comeback to the side. The 19-member team, to be led by Abhimanyu Easwaran, also features experienced pacer Mohammed Shami. Bengal will also get the service of pacer Mukesh Kumar, who will join the team on his return from India ‘A’ side’s tour of New Zealand. All-rounder Shahbaz Ahmed, who has been named in the India ‘A’ squad, will play Bengal’s opening match against Karnataka on Nov 14 before flying out to Doha for the Rising Stars Asia Cup tournament. Bengal have been placed in group ‘A’ alongside Karnataka, Chandigarh, Jharkhand, Mizoram, Baroda, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. All the group ‘A’ league matches will be held in Mumbai. Bengal squad: Abhimanyu Easwaran (capt.), Sudip Gharami, Yuvraj Keswani, Aditya Purohit, Abishek Porel (wk), Shakir Gandhi (wk), Karan Lal, Pradipta Pramanik, Sourav Halder, Prayas Ray Barman, Mohammed Shami, Mukesh Kumar, Shahbaz Ahmed, Kanishk Seth, Sayan Ghosh, Syed Irfan Aftab, Akhilesh Yadav, Rishabh Chaudhary and Shashank Singh.

item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Goalless draw in Braunschweig as Cottbus’ winless run stretches to six games
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Goalless draw in Braunschweig as Cottbus’ winless run stretches to six games Eintracht Braunschweig and Energie Cottbus drew goalless after an uneventful encounter at the start of matchday 11 in the 2. Bundesliga. The hosts had a strong start with Max Marie's blocked attempt inside the first minute of the game before striker Jovan Mijatovic tested Marcel Lotka on his first start since matchday 6. Braunschweig's momentum continued until Christian Kinsombi hit the post with a brilliant effort at the other end. Despite a similar start after the break from Lars Kornetka's side, Cottbus managed to slow down their hosts in their way of picking up their fifth draw of the campaign. Claus-Dieter Wollitz’s men will now go into the international break with a six-game winless run. Braunschweig stretched their clean sheet record to three successive home games, but they did win the previous two against Holstein Kiel and Hannover. The two teams joined five other clubs who collected 11 points before the rest of action this weekend. Both would face promotion hopefuls on matchday 11 as Braunschweig will travel to second-placed Nürnberg before Cottbus host league leaders Hertha BSC the following day.

item.title: Browns Coach Sends Strong Message About Shedeur Sanders
item.description: The Cleveland Browns are set to get their first look at Shedeur Sanders in his second season on Sunday afternoon against the New Orleans Saints on the road. Deshaun Watson is set to miss this week’s game due to a concussion. That has given Sanders a chance to get on the field and show what he’s capable of producing after a full offseason of development. Sanders showed some signs of starting potential during his rookie season. He also had his fair share of bad moments. When all was said and done in 2025, Sanders played in eight games and completed 56.6 percent of his pass attempts for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. Sanders also ran for 169 yards and a touchdown. This week, he’ll attempt to show enough to force head coach Todd Monken to keep him on the field moving forward. Speaking of Monken, the head coach spoke out about Sanders taking the field this week. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (2) warms up before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Browns’ Todd Monken Sends Honest Message About Shedeur Sanders As shared by ESPN’s Daniel Oyefus, Monken made it clear that he is excited to see Sanders on the field this week. “I’m fired up to see him play,” Monken said . “I mean, who wouldn’t be?” If things go well for Sanders this week, he could force Monken to make a difficult decision. At 24 years old, the former Colorado standout is still capable of being a long-term option for the Browns. Cleveland needs to find out what it truly has in Sanders before the end of the season. On the flip side, if things go poorly, the Browns will easily be able to shift back to Watson for the next game. Since being drafted, Sanders has become one of the most talked about players in the NFL. He has also been included in trade rumors leading up to the Tuesday deadline. A strong performance could help Cleveland move him if the franchise chooses to do so. Only time will tell what the future has in store for the son of the legendary Deion Sanders. Kickoff on Sunday is scheduled for 1:00 p.m ET against the Saints. Sanders will look to prove that he deserves to have a long future with the Browns. item.title: Red Wings embarking on rugged — and crucial — road trip
item.description: DETROIT — All the games are important, especially in the early stages of the regular season as teams adjust and build and head into the deeper parts of the schedule. The Red Wings, by points or win percentage — whatever way you prefer at this point of the season — were last in the Atlantic Division entering games Friday, Nov. 6. Now, it was closely bunched, for sure, but several teams also had played a game or two less than the Wings. You don't want to fall behind, and drift away from the teams ahead of the race. Which makes this upcoming four-game road trip, starting Saturday, Nov. 7, in Colorado (9 p.m./DSN/97.1), have the feel of a crucial week for the Wings. They face four quality teams — Colorado, St. Louis, then back to Florida and Tampa Bay — and the Wings have to earn some points, because otherwise, it'll be a game of catchup in the standings. And the way this division is shaping up, there may not be many teams who drift back to the pack. "We're going to play quality teams," coach Todd McLellan said. To be successful against these elite teams, the Wings will need generally better starts than they've had recently, plus finish some of these games better than they've had. The Wings are heading into this trip coming off a disheartening late-game 2-1 loss, Thursday, Nov. 5 to Vegas . A couple of defensive mistakes in the third period erased a 1-0 lead and stung the Wings. "Very disappointing, obviously," defenseman Moritz Seider said of the Vegas loss. "That can't be the standard of this locker room. It's been multiple times that we kind of just gave away the game in the last couple minutes, and that's not acceptable." McLellan laid out specific ways for the Wings to be successful on this road swing. "We can't shoot ourselves in the foot in these games," McLellan said. "If we put ourselves in good position, we have to find ways to close it out. We've done in Florida and Edmonton (both victories), against some real good teams. (Thursday) was a real good game, where the last one to make a mistake but we're going to play quality teams." Once the Wings conclude this stretch Nov. 14 in Tampa, they'll have only five more road games up until Christmas. It would be promising to accumulate some points this coming week, with a home-heavy schedule ahead of them. "It's been a strange start to the year for a lot of different reasons obviously," McLellan said. "The schedule, with so many home games (to start) and now a chunk of road games. "We have to go out there and get off to good starts. We need some production from key people, so when they get their looks and touches, they're going to have to produce. Our special teams and penalty kill has been improving and they have to stay at level. Our power play has to get us something." item.title: Real Madrid star beats Lamine Yamal to La Liga Player of the Month
item.description: Real Madrid star beats Lamine Yamal to La Liga Player of the Month Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé has officially beaten out the stiff competition to the award for La Liga’s Player of the Month for October. Frontman Mbappé for his part carried his stellar form in front of goal through last month. All told, across a trio of appearances in Spain’s top-flight, the Frenchman found the net four times. This included a decisive brace in Real Madrid’s crucial victory over arch rivals Barcelona. Such exploits proved enough to earn for Mbappé a place on the shortlist for La Liga Player of the Month, alongside the quartet of Lamine Yamal, Alejandro Grimaldo, Gonçalo Guedes and Matías Dituro. And as alluded to above, on Friday, Real Madrid’s star goalscorer has officially scooped the prize. On the same day in which Jude Bellingham was named Los Blancos’ Player of the Month, Mbappé has been named the best performer in Spain’s top-flight for October. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Wisconsin Football: Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely Scenarios vs. Rutgers
item.description: IOWA CITY, IA - OCTOBER 31: Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Ryan Hopkins (10) passes during a Big Ten Conference college football game between the Wisconsin Badgers and the Iowa Hawkeyes on October 31, 2026, at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, IA. (Photo by Keith Gillett/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Well, Iowa City happened. In what some have called the most disappointing loss of the Luke Fickell era, the Wisconsin Badgers were bludgeoned by an Iowa Hawkeyes team that simply wanted it more on the way to a humiliating 30-point drubbing, robbing all the goodwill Wisconsin had banked the week before by beating then-No. 16 USC 24-7. So, what is this Wisconsin team? Are they good? Bad? Mediocre? Maddeningly inconsistent? I’d say yes to all, and do so not even knowing who will start at quarterback against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights this weekend. I mean, Wisconsin should win . But they should have stayed within 30 points of Iowa, too. I simply don’t know when the next malodorous egg gets laid by this up-and-down squad. With all those positives out of the way, let’s turn to my Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely Scenarios for Badgers/Scarlet Knights. Best Case The cynic in me says this would be Wisconsin not getting embarrassed, but I’m going to aim a bit higher here. I see a world where the Badgers come in angry and wounded after getting ridiculously pantsed at Iowa and really take it to Rutgers. While I don’t think this offense is capable of putting up big numbers, we finally see some chunk plays, keyed by whoever starts at quarterback (my money is on the freshman), while the defense creates a few turnovers and generally has their way with an offense missing its best player, stud wide receiver KJ Duff. Prediction: Wisconsin 30-10. Worst Case I feel the need for a disclaimer here: I don’t think this will happen. But it’s a worst-case thing, so here we are. In this ghastly series of events, an Iowa hangover coupled with uncertainty at quarterback (and along the offensive line with Kevin Heywood out ) combine to make what should be an easy win a dicey slog. Rutgers, playing loose and with nothing to lose, come in a bit like Maryland did in 2025 and punch the Badgers in the mouth all day. Just two weeks from being ranked, the talk will all turn to Luke Fickell’s suddenly scalding hot seat. Prediction: Rutgers 23-16. Most Likely While I briefly toyed with an upset here, I remembered we have Mason Posa and Cooper Catalano. Tough-guy warriors like that duo are likely at the forefront of team talk this week, and I suspect the message gets across. It isn’t pretty in the least, but the Badgers simply find a way to get it done and come out with a stressful but important victory over the overmatched Scarlet Knights, led by a big turnover and Abu Sama’s best game as a Badger. Bowl eligibility is here after a two-year hiatus. Prediction: Wisconsin 23-16.

item.title: Barcelona coach wants to keep two La Masia wonderkids very close to the first team
item.description: Barcelona coach wants to keep two La Masia wonderkids very close to the first team According to SPORT , Hansi Flick has identified Ebrima Tunkara and Orian Goren as two Barcelona academy prospects that he wishes to keep close to the senior team. However, at the same time, the German tactician is in no rush to push either of them into the spotlight right away and intends to take a measured approach with their integration. Goren and Tunkara make an impression during pre-season Goren, 17, has already established himself as an important player for Barça Atletic. Despite still being a second-year youth player, the midfielder is a regular under Juliano Belletti, playing six games and registering two assists. On the back of his performances, the teenager has earned his maiden national team call-up with Israel . He was the academy youngster who lasted the longest in Flick’s first-team group during pre-season. Orian Goren is rated highly by Flick. (Picture courtesy: Instagram/@orian_goren) The La Masia talent was also involved in the Joan Gamper Trophy match and played a few minutes in the Catalans’ traditional curtain-raiser for the season. As for Tunkara, the 16-year-old attacking midfielder is widely regarded as the next most exciting talent coming through La Masia after Lamine Yamal . Despite his age and the fact that he is still a first-year youth player, the youngster has been handed the No. 10 shirt at Barça Atletic, for whom he has one assist in three games this term. He also featured prominently in the pre-season with the first team and made a big impression. “Ebrima Tunkara and Orian Goren have really impressed me during this training camp; they’re incredibly talented and are proving it,” Flick had said about the pair during pre-season. Ebrima Tunkara is one of La Masia’s most exciting talents. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Knocking on the first-team doors Tunkara and Goren’s involvement with the Barcelona senior team has not been limited to pre-season. As injuries created openings in the senior squad in recent weeks, both players began appearing in Flick’s matchday squads. Goren was included in the squad for El Clasico against Real Madrid and more recently in the UEFA Champions League clash against Aston Villa. Meanwhile, Tunkara was named in the squad for the La Liga match against Alaves. However, UEFA rules restrict him from appearing for the first team in the Champions League. For now, Flick’s plan is to keep both players involved with the first-team group in training regularly while ensuring that they get minutes playing for Barça Atletic.

item.title: Texas Southern got $25K for facing LSU. Was it worth it after a record loss?
item.description: The Texas Southern Tigers were on the wrong side of history on Thursday against the LSU Tigers. (Elias Valverde II/Dallas Morning News) The Texas Southern Tigers women's basketball team was on the wrong side of history on Thursday night. The Tigers traveled to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to face the No. 9 LSU Tigers. LSU won 131-22, the largest margin of victory in Division I women's basketball history against a Division I opponent, according to ESPN. Kim Mulkey, LSU's coach known for her unapologetic, flamboyant style, broke a record she set 10 years ago at Baylor. In 2016, Baylor beat Winthrop by 108 points in a decisive 140-32 blowout. The regrettable, history-making night also served as a homecoming for LSU alumna and WNBA superstar Angel Reese, who wore Chanel from head to toe, while Texas Southern served as mere background fodder for LSU's de facto homecoming night for their beloved former superstar. Texas Southern was outscored 40-0 in the second quarter, with seven LSU players scoring 10 or more points. Texas Southern's top scorer, Jayla Cornelius, tallied just 6 points in the loss. After the game, Reese and Mulkey joined their top stars at the press conference, and not one reporter even mentioned the record-setting night. It was like Texas Southern wasn't even there. How much did Texas Southern receive to play LSU So what did Texas Southern get out of the deal? Chron obtained the game contract from LSU, as Texas Southern received $25,000 for the contest. According to an On3 report by Andy Kitty, which studied 384 "money games" from the 2022-23 regular season, the record for the school that received the guarantee payment was just 16-368, or a 4.1 winning percentage. For Texas Southern, LSU and college basketball at large, was any of this worth it? Beyond giving players at the bottom of each team's roster some playing time, the game served as a scrimmage for two teams on opposite ends of the women's college hoops spectrum. LSU is considered one of the best teams in the country, coming off a Sweet 16 appearance last season. Meanwhile, Texas Southern finished near the bottom of the SWAC standings last season. Vernette Skeete is in her sixth season as head coach of the Texas Southern Lady Tigers. (Carly Mackler/Getty Images) LSU shouldn't apologize for being so good, and Texas Southern shouldn't apologize for being a program trying to find their way. But as they say in boxing, weight classes exist for a reason, and a lightweight has no business fighting a heavyweight. But for $25,000, was this worth the psychological impact for student-athletes (who are not likely receiving NIL) after a devastating loss? How does a program's brand and image suffer from making such infamous headlines? Recruiting future players to Texas Southern just became that much more difficult after Thursday's streamrolling by LSU. item.title: 2. Bundesliga: Dresden off the bottom with convincing victory over Fürth
item.description: 2. Bundesliga: Dresden off the bottom with convincing victory over Fürth First half goals from Robert Wagner and Ben Bobzien had the hosts firmly in control at the half. Vincent Vermeij added a second-half strike to make it 3-0 before Hendry Blank saw red for the visitors capping off a miserable evening for Fürth. Dresden made a lively start at the Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion, although Greuther Fürth initially looked dangerous going forward. The visitors came close to opening the scoring through Omar Sillah, whose effort drifted narrowly wide after a defensive mix-up, before Sacha Bansé tested Lennart Grill with a powerful effort from distance. Dynamo also threatened at the other end, with Patrice Čović missing a promising opportunity from inside the penalty area. However, it was the hosts who eventually broke the deadlock in the 31st minute. Niklas Hauptmann did well to turn away from two opponents before laying the ball into the path of Robert Wagner, whose first-time effort took a deflection off Hendry Blank and wrong-footed goalkeeper Florian Hellstern. Dynamo doubled their advantage ten minutes later, with Ben Bobzien finding the net in similarly fortunate circumstances. After receiving the ball from Tobias Raschl, the forward cut inside before seeing his effort deflected by Blank and loop into the top corner, leaving Hellstern with little chance of making a save. Fürth almost reduced the deficit before the interval, with Sillah narrowly missing a cross from Gian-Luca Itter before the latter saw two efforts blocked and deflected wide. Despite those opportunities, Thomas Stamm's side headed into the break with a deserved two-goal advantage. The hosts continued to apply pressure after the restart and effectively put the contest beyond doubt in the 55th minute. Bobzien turned provider this time, setting up Vincent Vermeij, who had the simple task of rolling the ball into an unguarded net to make it 3-0. Fürth's evening then went from bad to worse seven minutes later when Blank received his marching orders. Having already been booked in the opening minute, the defender brought down Bobzien as he threatened to break through on goal, receiving a second yellow card and leaving the visitors with ten men for the remainder of the contest. Dresden looked increasingly comfortable against their numerical disadvantage, with Čović coming close to adding a fourth in the 73rd minute, only for his effort to be blocked by Krisztián Keresztes close to the goal line. The hosts ultimately saw out a convincing 3-0 victory, recording another impressive home result following their recent wins over Magdeburg and in the cup against Schalke. The three points also provide a significant boost to Dresden's hopes of climbing away from the bottom of the 2. Bundesliga table, while Fürth will be disappointed with an evening in which defensive misfortune and Blank's dismissal contributed to a heavy defeat.

item.title: Friday Cheese Curds: Packers are plagued by missed opportunities
item.description: (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers don’t appear to have a problem finding open receivers. Receivers catching the ball, however, is unfortunately a problem. We’ve seen the stat six hundred times already, but here it is once more for posterity: Through eight games, Green Bay has recorded 23 dropped passes, eight more than any other NFL team. And don’t look now, but that’s already more than the Packers had all of last season. As Jordan Love continues to put together an outstanding year, drops are becoming impossible to ignore. The biggest surprise in all of this is Matthew Golden, who was drafted in part specifically because he is incredibly sure-handed. In his first training camp, months removed from a season where Packers receivers again struggled to make tough catches, Golden reportedly caught everything. In 2026, he has nine drops. But this isn’t exclusively a Golden problem. The issue has spread throughout a receiving group that has otherwise demonstrated plenty of big-play potential. Ok, let’s stop piling on. There’s reason for optimism. Christian Watson and Golden have shown the ability to make tough catches generate explosive plays. Tucker Kraft has, too — and I’d expect him to start accumulating impressive plays as he continues to regain confidence following a return from a knee injury. The talent is there, we’ve seen the proof before, and Love clearly has confidence in his receivers. That’s what makes the problem so frustrating. Green Bay doesn’t necessarily need to find another receiver before the November 10 trade deadline. It needs the very talented receivers already on the roster to catch the dang ball. Until then, they’ll continue to be a streaky offense with a quarterback leading the league in passing yards. If the pass catchers can turn it around, though, the passing attack could graduate to the “most dangerous in the league” conversation. That’ll also be necessary for this team to survive the NFC North and do damage in the playoffs. I dunno, can we go back to making them catch bricks or something? Packers lead NFL in drops by a huge margin The Green Bay Packers currently hold a wide and possibly insurmountable lead for dropped passes as the midway point of the 2026 season approaches. Packers must be buyers at trade deadline The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday. The Packers haven’t been buyers in a long time but there is a green-and-golden opportunity to make a move in the wide-open NFC. item.title: Browns’ Deshaun Watson finally returns to practice, but what does that mean for Shedeur Sanders?
item.description: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Browns’ Deshaun Watson finally returns to practice, but what does that mean for Shedeur Sanders? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol, the door is open for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season for the team on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. As S anders prepares for the potential start with the Browns , the latest update on Watson could bring a cloud of confusion around the status of both quarterbacks. According to team insider Mary Kay Cabot at Cleveland.com, Watson returned to practice on Friday after being absent for the past two days with the concussion. However, he is “not fully cleared” and is still in the concussion protocol, with the reporter saying that Sanders “still has a good chance to start.” UPDATE: Cleveland head coach Todd Monken announced Friday that Sanders will start against the Saints, per Andrew Siciliano. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “ Shedeur Sanders will start at QB for the Browns Sunday, per Todd Monken,” Siciliano wrote on X. “Deshaun Watson is questionable, but still hasn’t cleared concussion protocol.” Browns’ Todd Monken on Shedeur Sanders’s preparation Sanders has been waiting for the chance to start for the Browns since the offseason, as he was competing with Watson for the role, as it inevitably went to the veteran. Now with the chance to prove himself to Cleveland, Monken would reveal how Sanders has prepared, saying he has “done his work.” “All he’s done is be diligent and ask great questions. In every meeting, he’s dialed in, and he’s willing to talk to me about certain things or the rest of the players. During the game, he’s talking to the guys. … That’s why I said I’m so excited to see him today. That’s what you do. Doesn’t matter whoever takes the field; that represents the Cleveland Browns, there’s an expectation in the position of how you’re going to play, and we’ll hold him to that,” Monken said Wednesday, via Kay Cabot. #Browns Todd Monken on why he’s excited to see what Shedeur Sanders can do: pic.twitter.com/Bic3i7RWzP — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) November 4, 2026 At any rate, it remains to be seen how Watson progresses up until Sunday afternoon’s game against the Saints, but fans should expect Sanders to be under center as the team is 5-3, putting them third in the tough AFC North.
